title: India Tells Nationals in Saudi Arabia: Stay Off Balconies and Rooftops, Call 911 or 998 in an Emergency
excerpt: The Indian Embassy in Riyadh on October 18 relayed updated Saudi Civil Defense directives — move to an interior room away from windows, do not photograph strikes, and pull over away from bridges if driving — after the October 10 airport attack that killed an Indian national.
body:
• Emergency numbers: call 911 in Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh and the Eastern Province, and 998 everywhere else in Saudi Arabia if you face a threat or danger.
  • When an alert sounds, move at once to an interior room away from windows and glass, stay off balconies and rooftops, and do not leave the building until the danger has passed.
  • Do not photograph or film strikes or share such images: the Indian Embassy in Riyadh, relaying updated Saudi Civil Defense directives on October 18, repeated a ban on filming and publishing material about the attacks.
  • If you are driving when an alert arrives, pull over away from bridges and high-rise buildings; if you are outdoors, enter the nearest building or shelter behind a solid barrier.

The Indian Embassy in Riyadh on Sunday urged Indian nationals across Saudi Arabia to follow updated safety directives issued by Saudi authorities, as Houthi drone and missile attacks on the kingdom continued. The embassy relayed instructions tied to warnings issued through Saudi Arabia's National Early Warning Platform for Emergencies, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

What to Do When an Alert Sounds

Stay calm, follow directions from official channels, and move immediately to the nearest safe place inside a building, preferably an interior room away from windows, the directives say. People should not leave their homes or buildings until the threat subsides, should stay away from open areas, windows and glass, and should not stand on balconies or rooftops.

The guidance also tells people to avoid crowds and dangerous areas and to refrain from taking photographs. The Times of India reported the same list on Sunday: remain indoors, keep away from glass, and wait for competent authorities to signal through official channels that the danger has passed.

If You Are Outdoors or Driving

Anyone caught outdoors during an alert should enter the nearest building or take shelter behind a solid barrier, the directives say. Drivers who receive an alert should pull over to the side of the road, away from bridges and high-rise buildings, and wait there rather than continuing toward a destination.

In an emergency, the number depends on where you are. Call 911 in Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh and the Eastern Province. Call 998 in the rest of Saudi Arabia. Both numbers were listed in the Saudi instructions the embassy shared on its social media channels.

Why the Embassy Updated Its Guidance

The October 18 update follows a deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on October 10. That attack killed an Indian national and injured several other people, and it prompted the embassy to issue its first round of safety advice in this sequence.

Immediately after the October 10 strike, the embassy had already urged Indian nationals to follow local authorities' instructions, remain indoors during aerial attacks, and refrain from filming, publishing or sharing information, photographs or videos related to the events. Sunday's message adds the fuller Civil Defense list, including the interior-room instruction, the driving rule, and the two emergency numbers.

Saudi Arabia has faced repeated drone and missile attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels in recent weeks, and Saudi emergency warnings are now a recurring feature of daily life in Riyadh and other cities. For Indian workers and families, that makes the alert routine worth rehearsing before an alert arrives: know which room in the home or workplace is farthest from windows, keep phones charged so Early Warning Platform alerts are heard, and save 911 or 998 depending on your region.

What Indian Nationals Should Do Now

Follow only official Saudi and Indian Embassy channels for instructions, rather than social media rumours about strike locations. Do not go to a rooftop or balcony to watch interceptions, do not drive toward an incident, and do not photograph or circulate images of impacts or military activity.

Anyone travelling inside Saudi Arabia should factor alerts into the journey, and families should agree in advance where to gather inside the home if a warning sounds at night. The embassy has not announced any evacuation, and Sunday's advisory is a safety instruction, not a departure order.
